listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Tuesday, October 13, 2026. The lead story is about Pope Leo. The Vatican said he had successful surgery to remove a lower lobe of his right lung. The Vatican also said he was diagnosed with lung cancer. The surgery was successful, according to the Vatican. Now the front stories. Six Democratic and six Republican senators wrote to President Trump. They asked him to withdraw from his recent diesel deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump removed Kimberly Guilfoyle as US ambassador to Greece after corruption allegations. She called the allegations false. Pakistan has imposed emergency rule in the province governed by the party of imprisoned former prime minister Imran Khan. Georgia Tech has unveiled Nexus, a next-generation AI supercomputer for researchers across the country. Now, one short sentence for each section. In Tech and AI, Anthropic is expanding its Cyber Verification Program for security professionals. In Politics, The Lever looks at Medicare for All and at Senator Sheldon Whitehouse's plan for a future Democratic president. In World, US diesel prices hit an all-time high in September. In Sports, Brendan Allen won a fifth-round submission in the UFC. In Atlanta, the WNBA Finals games three and four will be played at State Farm Arena. In Architecture, GPT-6 Astra is being tested as a 3D modeller for BIM. In Science and Nature, a Voyager lunar lander passed environmental tests at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Pope diagnosed with lung cancer but had successful surgery, Vatican says
lead.note: The Vatican said Pope Leo was diagnosed with lung cancer and had successful surgery to remove a lower lobe of his right lung. The announcement is the main news on this day's brief. Surgery is a significant event for any patient, and the Vatican's statement is the primary source for these details. The summary does not describe his recovery plans or any further treatment, so those remain unknown from this report. The story is included as the most widely significant item in today's selection. Readers can follow later updates from the Vatican for details beyond the initial announcement.
